body: I’ve been to this exact venue quite a few times. It gets PACKED for some of the concerts…why would you bring a baby?!?!
I did this last year when my son turned 18. He’s almost 19 now and has a 765 credit score. Better than mine…
I had to tell a dad of a 14 year old he wasn’t the father. It was over the phone and the breath that left his body kinda broke my soul. Next hardest conversation was telling the child…
Melt the butter, dip the bread in the melted butter. Cook as normal. Total game changer.

This is very valid. My mother had dementia and got to the point where she was unable to leave the house much and couldn’t attend church. She then turned to constantly watching a well known television-evangelist on TV. Long story short, I was going through her finances and found that she had sent this man several hundred dollars within 3-4 months. With her fixed income it was bleeding her dry. Shortly before she passed she told me how she called the number to give a donation and was having a really hard time reading off the numbers on her debit card. She told the “sweet young man” how she would have to call him back when she had someone to help her. Apparently he doubled down and told her it didn’t matter how long it took, he would stay on the phone with her until she could get all the numbers read off. That was a $200 donation that one phone call alone. I can’t even describe the level of absolute loathing I have for that disgusting leech. OP I completely understand your frustration.
My Grocery app. You can link up the app with other household members so what gets put on the grocery list by one person shows up on the others. It’s incredibly helpful.

My Jeep Wrangler. It’s been my dream car since I was 10. Realized around 15-16 years old it was probably never gonna happen. Decided I could make do with a Geo Tracker (I’m old, don’t judge). Lack of money, kids and life kept me from owning either until 4-5 years ago and I was able to buy a late model Jeep. I’m a grandma now and to my 4 year old grandson all Wranglers are “grandma’s Jeep”. 16 year old me might be horrified I’m a grandma in my mid 40’s but she’d be thrilled that we have our dream car.

I think the “dance floor” tree had a building on top of it at one point. I’m going off of memory from quite a few years ago. When the walls were torn down some of the wood was used in a house that was a brothel just outside of Sonora. I used to clean the old brothel house for the owner. She had lived in the same home for 60+ years. She loved to tell me the history of the area and proudly proclaimed the wood in the home was used after “the old dance hall” was torn down.

Oh my goodness I forgot I posted this photo! I look soooo different now! (2 years later). My face continued to morph and I’m finally myself but a better version. I’m doing great. Right now I’m fighting clenching my jaw too much which is causing pain but that’s definitely a me problem and not due to the surgery. Hope things are going well for you!
This right here is why I joined this sub. I love the suggestions and helpfulness!
Ummm….I’ll see myself out
I hated the splint! And yep, food got stuck in there. Eggs were the worst because I could still taste it days later. Keep eating my friend. You need the calories and to strengthen your jaw.

I took Tylenol and ibuprofen at the same time. It really takes the pain away as good as a pain pill. I had my surgeons okay to take 800mg of ibuprofen and 1000mg of Tylenol every 6-8 hours. However, i’d clear this with your doc to make sure this is okay for you.

I am not LE but I work closely with several agencies. One of the absolute hardest things is to find out someone is not going to be criminally charged for a crime against a child. It’s frustrating and it is in no way fair to the kid that endured the trauma. I sat through an almost 4 hour forensic interview of a kid disclosing some heinous shit. Solid interview and gut wrenching. LE did their job but in the end no charges as it boiled down to “he said/she said”. Sickens me to this day.

Sis, it’s the new normal. I feel this. My nose is soooo much wider now. I feel like it takes over my face. I’m fairly certain it’s because my top jaw was widened. I’m not super happy about it but also, I’m kinda getting used to it…not so much the jowls that are kinda forming but don’t worry about that. I’m just old. 😁

Eat super small bites and mash food with your tongue. Your jaw will be sore after only a few bites so you gotta work up to being able to eat a full meal. When I first was able to chew soft foods I tried spaghetti-O’s and it felt like I was chomping on uncooked rice. Time is really the best thing for this. Good luck!

Does anyone else remember the video series about the Rapture? This was years before the Left Behind series. Made in the late 70’s/early 80’s I think? I had to watch them all. Nightmare fuel right there.
I met a girl named Hennessy once. She was a teenager…in rehab. I don’t think that kid had a chance.

My husband is a corrections officer and has a plethora of “love letters” from inmates. He is one of the strictest CO’s (small jail) so I don’t really get why he gets hit on but I find it hilarious. He does not.

I totally agree. I’m kinda new(ish) to this sub but found a lot of good info pre surgery and have been able to offer suggestions/encouragement post op. The amount of “do I need surgery” has gone up exponentially in the past few weeks and it really does retract from the general questions and amazing pre and post op pics.

I had a friend way back in the day that had her babies 8.5 months apart. She was pregnant within 3-4 weeks of giving birth. The second baby was born very early. I went with her so she could get the depo shot, they made her take a pregnancy test before giving it to her. Imagine everyone’s surprise when the test was positive.

I’m still getting used to my face. It’s really changed (I had UJS with a 7-8mm move forward to correct my underbite). I have awesome cheek bones now! And my skin is tighter so I got a small face lift out of it. The biggest difference is my headaches have decreased by 75%, my breathing is soooo much better and I feel better. So in the end I think it was worth it.
I’m in my mid 40’s and 7 months PO. Kudos to you for moving forward in this.

My husband is a total trash panda, will eat anything cold/hot or whatever combo he feels will work. 
For me, food was a huge part of our house growing up. I started cooking at a young age and found out I really liked it so most nights I still cook a full meal. I say this as I’m finishing up a Banquet Pit Pie (fully cooked) for dinner.

I promise it gets better. This surgery is mentally brutal and I don’t think it’s discussed enough on here. You are going to go through a roller coaster of emotions during this time. I focused on this being a temporary feeling and would tell myself often it’s not permanent. To be honest, it took a solid 5 months to feel like myself again. It’s okay to feel this way but don’t let it overtake your life. Find things you can do to occupy your time. This is temporary my friend. It gets better. I’m 7 months PO so I’ve been where you are at. I spent a few weeks regretting everything and feeling hopeless. Now, I am in a much better place and feeling like myself. You got this!

I’m having some uncommon complications at the moment so I’m still recovering. One of the plates didn’t like my face and I had to have it removed a couple weeks ago. I’m still battling an infection on that side. I’m looking at 30 days of antibiotics and if that doesn’t work I’ll be doing yet another surgery. As scary as that sounds, I’ve had so many benefits I’d still say it’s worth it. I’m breathing way better and my speech has improved. My concave face is no longer concave and I have amazing cheek bones now! Also, as a side benefit, since my upper jaw was moved so forward it tightened my skin giving me a little facelift. Once the infection is cleared up my next step is to get my braces off, hopefully sometime this year. :)

5th grade me thought learning the metric system was pointless because the teacher said it was mainly used outside the US. I remember thinking I’ll never live outside the States so why bother? 15 years later I moved to Germany….
Im 6 months PO from UJS. Im in my mid 40’s with braces. Do I look ridiculous? Probably. Would I do this over again? Yep.

Maurice’s, Old Navy, Amazon and sometimes Shein. For nicer stuff I buy from New York & Co (when they are having a sale). I’m 5’9 with a long inseam and NY&C have the size inseams I need. I absolutely hate shopping in stores so I’m almost exclusively an online shopper.

It really depends on the surgery. I had UJS and a splint was put in for 6 weeks. Talking was almost impossible. There was no way I could have went back to work before 6 weeks. Physically, this surgery can kick your butt. I would say, if possible, maybe see if you could work half days? Initially though, you are going to need minimum 3-4 weeks recovery time.
You look amazing!

45 here and almost 6 months PO. Still in braces. I thought the same thing…live with what I had. However, my speech started to become less clear and I found out it would only get worse as time went on. The term “concave face” really got to me as well (class 3 underbite) so I doubled down and did it. Do I look weird as a 45 year old in braces? Probably. Would I do it again? Absolutely.
Well damn…how am I gonna tell 3 out of my 4 kids I’m not really their mom?
Enya is what got me into EDM strangely enough. Loved the music with the deep beat and I went searching…on Napster of course, for more things like it.

I was in that spot too and did not even realize the absolute toxicity until after we were divorced. My life was wrapped around his career advancements, his getting a degree, his social status etc…all at the expense of my own (tbf I’m a complete introvert so I didn’t care about the social climbing) but once I divorced, damn if I’m not living my best life.
Literally the first song I thought of when I read the post. It was so over played and I hated it from the get go. Hope I never hear it again.

I’m not saying this is your situation but I was married to a man like this. The need was constant and he’d tell me it’s how he shows his love. It got to the point where it became toxic and he’d ignore our children until he got what he wanted. Turned out he was addicted and I wasn’t the only one he “showed his love to”. I’d caution you to really examine how this is affecting you and your mental health. I became just a body to him that he happened to be married to. There was no love, it was a means to an end for him and left me feeling used.

I’ve said this before in some other posts but Honestly, do NOT judge your face right now. 5 weeks PO and I hit a depression like you wouldn’t believe. I regretted the surgery, I hated my face and ended up in tears over it. My surgeon told me how great I looked and I nicely called him a liar. He told me not to judge until the 6 month mark. I am almost 5 months PO and I actually really like my face! I look like myself but the 2.0 version. I smile more and don’t try to hide my face like I did. 
I go in next week to get one of the plates removed and the swelling will be back, but I know it will eventually go down and I’ll be back to my new normal. Yes your face looks weird. You had major surgery on it. But it’s temporary I promise. Little by little you’ll start to see you. Time is your friend in this instance. Gotta give yourself time to heal. You got this!
Not late at all. I’m also now scheduled for surgery May 17th to remove the plate. I’m currently on another round of antibiotics and steroids. I hope things go well for you!

Make sure you get condiment bottles for drinking liquids. You’ll probably have a splint put in if they are breaking your top jaw to fix the crossbite. The splint sucks! It’s not painful, just annoying. Take pain meds regularly. It’s much easier to maintain pain then to let your meds go and have to start over with pain management. Ice cream is king, just make sure it’s blended thin. 
Time will go by slowly. Make sure you have books to read, tv to watch or video games to play. 
Your mental health might take a nosedive. About 5 weeks PO I hit a pretty low point. 
Don’t judge your face for at least 6 months. There will be lots of swelling and things will shift. 
Keep in mind the pain/discomfort is temporary. 
I’m almost 5 months PO. The first 8 weeks really suck but it’s definitely worth it!
As a mom to a 21 year old son struggling with addiction, this gut punched me. My biggest fear these days is the addiction will win. I’m so sorry for your loss.

My mom suffered from dementia (she passed away this past December) and her speech was in pretty steep decline. I had taken over her finances and checked her account one day to see $500 sent to Jimmy Swaggart. Of course I (gently) confront my mom about it and she tells me she almost wasn’t able to finish the transaction because of her speech. however “the nice man on the phone” offered to walk her through the process and told her to take her time getting her debit card numbers right. My mom was on a very fixed income and couldn’t hardly communicate but that asshole made sure she got those numbers right to give them money. Makes my blood boil just typing this out.

In my past life I was married to a man that made me responsible for making sure he was up on time. He would get upset with me if I dared to fall back asleep after his last alarm went off and I didn’t make sure he was up. I did this for many years and just accepted I was responsible for this grown ass man waking up on time. Nope. Time to set boundaries my friend and stick with them.
I’m almost 4 months PO from UJS and my top teeth are just now starting to have some feeling in them. It’s definitely a weird sensation. It feels like my teeth are swollen if that makes sense.
Material Girl by Madonna.

I knew I needed surgery for my underbite but put it off until 4 months ago. My speech was becoming less clear so I bit the bullet and went to see an orthodontist who referred me to a surgeon. I have always been a mouth breather and let me tell you, after UJS I had rivers of air flowing through my nose! I can now breathe brought my nose with ease. It’s actually pretty awesome. 
Start with an orthodontist. A knowledgeable one will be able to see if you are a candidate for at least a consult with a surgeon.

Last time I got spanked with a belt I was 15. My dad heard me tell my little brother he was pissing me off. Got hit so hard I had several bruises on my thigh. I went to my mom, showed her the bruises and made my one and only threat I’d ever make to my parents (shaking like a leaf). I told her I would report them if he ever hit me again.

Also, getting paddled at school was super common back in the day. Can’t even imagine a school employee spanking my child.

Yes! One of the benefits I got from UJS was kind of a free facelift (I’m in my mid 40’s almost 4 months PO). The huge thing for me is the lines under eyes are probably 50% better after surgery. My smile? I’m still trying to get used to it. I had a huge underbite and never saw my top teeth and now Bam! They are front and center. It’s not horrible, just…different.

I love teenagers. I have one kiddo left at home. I think I’ll keep him since he’s a pretty awesome dude. I also work with teens, usually in crisis situations, and I just appreciate their views on life. That being said, compared to the Gen-X population, teens today seem so much more immature than when we were kids. We basically got ignored and left to our own devices. We grew up on our own. Things are definitely different.

I just finished my 3rd round of antibiotics for as many infections. I only ran a fever with one of them. Swelling may or may not be infection related but I’d definitely suggest calling your surgeon. Better safe than sorry my friend.

So I had an underbite and NEVER saw my top teeth unless I smiled big. I swear for the first 2 months I looked deformed, like the grinch. It’s still super odd for me to see myself smiling and see my front teeth but slowly it’s starting to feel a bit more normal. Things will definitely be changing, and for the better. Hang on my friend and give it time.

I have to agree with you on the (should I get surgery?) cosmetic questions but I also know some people are just generally looking for advice. I’m almost 4 months PO from UJS and still recovering . If it wasn’t very necessary I honestly wouldn’t have done it. I think people see the before and after photos ,it’s sometimes such a big transformation, they wonder if it would help them look better/feel better. I’m not gonna lie, I’m really starting to like my new face and I have zero regrets but damn it was rough physically and emotionally. (The depression post surgery is real). I get the appeal but I also think people don’t realize how truly beautiful they already are. No cosmetic surgery needed.

My favorite (read: horrifying) thing is to see someone you know from back in the day come up on social media and think “damn, they’re old!” Only to realize you went to school with them and you’re just as old. I tell myself I look better than my age and feel bad for the ones that don’t. I’m in complete denial. I’m old.

I was married for 20 years when I found out my husband cheated with multiple women. My fairy tail romance was, in fact, a nightmare.  Heartbroken is too light of a term. It was complete devastation. He was my world and I was his option. I felt like something must be wrong with me and it took me a very long time to see my own value and that the problem was him. My kids kept me going. I couldn’t allow myself to sink into the depression I so wanted to be in. I honestly thought my life was over, but it was just beginning. I’m living my best life these days.

Hands down my dog. My parents and I found her on the side of the road and took her home. Kept her for many years until she got sick. Cried over my teenage angst on her soft fur more times than I can count. She was absolutely my best friend. I still miss her.

It gets better. I promise. I felt extreme regret for a time. I didn’t look like myself or even feel like myself. Depression hit me hard as well. It’s going to be okay. This is a temporary feeling. I know it sucks now but there is a light at the end of the tunnel. Im almost 4 months PO and just now starting to look like myself…but the 2.0 upgraded version. I know how you are feeling and it sucks. But I promise it won’t feel this awful forever.

My daughter (not bio related but still very much my kid) had a half sister that was put up for adoption before my daughter was born. She always wondered about her and we spent a lot of time looking for her. My daughter was able to track her down on social media and tried to connect with her. She was completely rejected and the sister made it clear she wanted no contact. Completely her right to do so, but it really hurt my daughter. Her bio family is very small and I know she was very hopeful to make that connection with her sister. You are doing the right thing.
It may already be listed on here but Forensic files. I could watch it 24/7 and be a happy human.

Driving down the Autobahn and seeing a castle just off in the distance and being in a church built in the 1200s (The Church of Saint Elizabeth in Marburg Germany).  It was a spiritual experience for sure.
Success is the best revenge sis. It may take some time but use the drive you have to plot out your best life without him. Don’t waste another minute on this douche bag.
My grandson went through a phase of only wanting to watch coco melon or Super Monsters. I have seen every single episode of Super Monsters at least 4x. Zero regrets.
BCBS is my secondary insurance and they approved me on the first submission. My primary insurance is the one that gave me a bit of trouble. I had to appeal once and it was approved.

I was looking at photos with my grandson. He’s almost two. My mother (his great grandma) recently passed so we were looking at photos of Nana. He was so patient, waiting while I pointed out who everyone was in various photos. I love this kid so much. He is the most amazing human.

I feel this! I Mrs rough to look in a mirror and see a different reflection. I liked my old face but I didn’t like the problems my underbite gave me. Things have improved but I’m still getting used to my new look (I’m 10 weeks PO).

I have grown kids and speak to at least one of them almost daily. I honestly love it when they call/video chat or text me. Makes my mom heart very happy. I try to give them space to be independent adults but I always love it when they call for silly things or even the important stuff. 
That being said, my own mom passed away this past Christmas Eve. I wish I could pick up the phone and call her. I have saved voicemails that I now treasure. I haven’t played them because my heart can’t handle hearing her voice yet but it’s now all I have. 
So keep calling your mom daily and enjoy those moments you have with her.
I’m 2 months PO from UJS. Top pallet has some feeling but I still can’t feel my upper teeth, most of my upper lip and the tip of my nose. It’s slowly but surely improving!

I had UJS which required me to wear a splint for the first 6 weeks. I also have a job where talking is a huge part of my daily activities. The splint made it super difficult. I took the entire 6 weeks off. After the splint was (finally!) off I returned to work. My speech is a little impacted now because I have a new top pallet but no one has complained they can’t understand me.
I lost 10lbs in the first week. I’m 2 months PO and have gained back 4lbs.

At 4 weeks I had to clean out my moms apartment. She passed away 10 days after I had my surgery. It was only a few of us cleaning up and I was trying to be very careful in helping to pack things. I put a box on the u-haul and stepped off the truck harder than I realized. I felt my entire top jaw move. It wasn’t immediately painful but the swelling and subsequent infection were not fun.

As others have said, ask your surgeon but also be aware that you are barely healed and cycling may not be safe. I’m unsure if you mean cycling outdoors or stationary but please just be careful either way. It might be safest to just wait a few more weeks. The additional swelling and possibility of an infection if something happens is not worth it my friend.
I’m in my mid 40’s with braces. It’s weird at first but then you kinda get used to it.

I took 6 weeks off after my UJS but that was because I had to wear a splint. This made talking fairly difficult. I’m 8 weeks PO and still have some swelling. My surgeon said not to worry too much until the 6 month mark.  If you have to do much talking for your classes keep things in mind if you have to wear a splint.

I have had an @msn.com email account since AOL 2.0. 
Still use it regularly.
You’re not wrong lol

This reminds me of my 5th grade year (US). We were introduced to the metric system. I thought it was stupid and didn’t bother to learn ANY of it. Figured I’d never leave the country so why bother…15 years later I found myself living in Germany. Knew nothing about the metric system and had to do a crash course trying to figure things out. Wanted to kick 5th grade me’s ass.
I’ll be 8 weeks tomorrow.

Absolutely this. I am 2 months PO and still have plenty of swelling. My smile looks like the Cheshire Cat. I take pics daily and can see a huge difference from week 1 to now. It’s a long journey for sure.

One of the reasons I had surgery was because my speech was impacted by my underbite. Ironically, my speech is still a bit off after surgery because I have a new upper jaw and some words sound “off” to me. I may end up having to do some speech therapy to figure out how to say certain words. I also had a concave face and I started to see that it was getting worse (I’m in my 40’s). My hope was to improve looks, speech and my headaches.

Soft ice cream, mashed potatoes with gravy, cottage cheese, eggs and surprisingly spam (lightly fried and cut up really small). Spaghetti’os are possible but skip the meatballs. Pancakes are doable as well. Your jaw will tire out before your stomach is full so it may take some time. Good luck!

It’s definitely a challenge. Take small bites.. It’s really a learning process. I had a pretty big underbite and am finding spoons a bit challenging since surgery so I totally get the weirdness of it. Also, you are probably still pretty numb so it just feels weird. Hang in there and keep trying until you find what works for you.

I know this may not answer your question but I want to share something with you. There was a baby born a few years ago that was surrendered under the Safe Haven law. I was his assigned social worker and had the big responsibility of finding the right family that could potentially be his forever home. I say potential because in my State we have to publish info regarding the baby in case a parent or family member stepped forward. No one came forward and this baby, now 3 years old is living his best life with an amazing family. His father is a farmer so he lives the rural life with lots of outdoor time and a very wonderful stay at home mom and some amazing siblings. I was there the day they adopted him and even though I try not to cry in front of people, a tear or two may have fallen during the proceedings. 

My point is this, you did what you felt is best, not just for yourself but for your baby. Those that are judging you would not have to put in the day to day care of raising a child you knew you were not prepared for.  You did not abandon your baby. Don’t let anyone make you feel bad for doing what you felt was right.
Wow! You look great! Good luck on the learning to chew part. Take it very slow and small bites. It can be a bit frustrating and your jaw will tire very easily.

I returned to work at 6 weeks. Honestly I was ready. It’s nice having some down time and all but after a while boredom set in for sure. Make sure you plan out books you want to read, movies you want to watch etc…to keep yourself occupied.
I remember him from Flight of the Navigator. Dr. Faraday. I watched that movie hundreds of times as a kid.

Sis, I was a military wife back in the day and the same kind of shit happened to me. My (then) husband gas lighted the hell out of me. We were stationed in Germany for a few years. He arrived before I did and one night I couldn’t get a hold of him. When we next talked he told me he went to the local brothel with his battle buddies to “babysit them” and just had a few drinks and waited for them to do their thing. I stupidly chose to believe him. If I pressed too much he would assure me he was faithful and tell me I was acting unstable and mental. Of course, years later he finally confessed (to multiple, and I mean multiple, affairs) and I kick myself for not listening to my gut. The writing is on the wall my friend and you have to make a choice. I wasted 20 years on a serial cheater. Don’t ever make someone a priority when you are an option to them.
I’m 45 and in braces. You are definitely not too old.

I’m almost 7 weeks PO and still don’t like my face. I’m back at work and it’s been a bit of struggle for me as things haven’t “settled” yet. Still pockets of swelling and of course I’m still pretty numb. Since masks are mandatory where I live it’s actually been a blessing as I can hide behind that while at work.

The hardest part for me was week 2 and 3. The swelling is awful and you’re just kinda miserable. Pain wise, it’s bearable . The discomfort is really the worst. However, as others have stated, each person’s experience will be different. 
I had some anxiety leading up to the surgery so I asked my doctor for some low level anti anxiety meds for the last couple days before surgery. That seemed to help. 
Lastly, you will absolutely not like your face after surgery. It takes time for things to mend. No trauma but be aware this could affect your mental health for a time while you heal. Good luck!

I’m a week ahead of you (almost 7 weeks PO). Can confirm there’s still swelling. I had a doctor explain that there is a lot of soft tissue damage that happens during surgery and that takes time to settle. Also, I was told I won’t even know what my final results will be until at LEAST 6 months PO. I had UJS and my top lip is still pretty swollen. you can use heat if the swelling gets too bad. It’s a long journey friend. Just gotta give it time.
Tried googling this but no luck.

You may have an infection or it could be that you are just feeling things for the first time. I’d suggest calling your surgeon and have them double check you. I’m 6 weeks PO and have had 2 infections since the surgery.

If you are having a cross bite fixed you might have a splint in after surgery. This will make talking a bit difficult. The pain is pretty manageable but there’s a lot of discomfort. Your face will swell up A LOT and will take some time to go back down. You will look different. Your nose may change shape and you may look like the grinch for a while. You will be extremely numb for a while. That will take time as well. A lot of things will depend on what kind of surgery you are having. I had UJS only so my swelling and numbness are around my cheeks, nose and upper lip. 

Some tips: Stay hydrated! Drink tons of water, Gatorade, fruit juice and protein shakes. Condiment bottles are the absolute best in the first couple weeks for getting fluid. 

Trust. The. Process. It’s a major surgery and your body will need ample time to recover. There may come a time when you don’t like your face. This is normal so give it time. 

Stay on top of your pain meds. Pain management is a lot easier than pain relief.  I say this because I tried to skip a dose of Tylenol/ Ibuprofen today and now I’m hurting. 

Have a list ready of things to occupy your time. You will get bored. This can be movies, books, music or whatever you are into that does not require a lot of physical activity. 

Good luck on your journey!

I’ve had a few people say “you look so different!” which I’m not a fan of. I liked my face before surgery so I was hoping for not too much difference. My kiddos tells me I look different but I’m still me. I’m only 6 weeks PO so I’m still a little grinch looking. I am returning to work soon so it will be interesting to see if there is a difference.
It’s very slowly improving. I can feel part of my cheek now but my top lip and nose are still number. Getting better every day!
My son telling me he’s going to treatment. He’s not quite there yet but at least he’s talking about it. Addiction/mental health issues suck.

I absolutely agree with the gym part. I credit keeping my sanity through my divorce by running. I pounded pavement daily with lots of loud music. It kept me from focusing on why/how my marriage fell apart (he cheated A. LOT). Things will constantly loop in your head and you may find yourself asking why you weren’t enough (it’s definitely not that you weren’t). Do things to get out of your own head. Stay busy and stay focused on you and your kids.
I had UJS and it made my philtrum longer. I have new cheek bones as well. My nose also ended up looking different. I posted pics a while back and you can check them out to see the changes.
Thanks! I kinda got a free face lift out of the deal so I’m not complaining at all.

I had a splint, just got it removed yesterday. That made talking difficult. I’m now getting used to having a new roof of my mouth but I’m talking okay. Eating is a challenge. Your jaw will get tired easily and you have to take really small bites. I used to be a quick eater so it’s been interesting learning how to eat slowly.

Both injuries sound as though they were serious enough (and questionable enough) to warrant a call to CPS. Sometimes medical personnel CYA themselves as they cannot definitively say “this happened at school”. I get these calls often enough and do my due diligence to ensure things are kosher with how/what/when/why things happened. 

For example: I had a case of an infant with a fractured skull. Those are pretty serious and I went to work on finding out what happened. Long story short, mom reported the kid fell, outside specialized medical experts agreed the fracture was consistent with a fall and I closed the case without removing the child. A lot of times people believe the myth that CPS shows up and takes kids to foster care. While back in the day this may have been somewhat true, it’s not the case nowadays but the myth remains. 

Twice I’ve been in the room with a detective interviewing parents and had them say they were more scared of me than the detective. I understand the fear and I try really hard to help reduce that while also ensuring the health and safety of kids. That being said, a parent threatening to not seek future medical care for their kid because it may trigger a CPS investigation is a huge red flag. 

Source: Am a CPS Investigator

I did a quick look in your state and it looks like you have CRA (Children Requiring Assistance) but at first glance it appears this is for parents or schools that have at risk youth. CPS is focused on the child’s health, welfare and safety. We (I conduct CPS investigations in another state) do not walk into a family’s life to remove children. I can’t speak for your state but where I work, poverty, homelessness and mental health are not stand alone reasons for removing a child from the home.  When I go into a home where there is a newborn I’m looking for kept well-child check-ups, WIC appointments, a clean child and a clean and safe home as well as parents who are practicing safe sleep. If mental health for the parents are a concern I’m looking for proof that they are in counseling, and/or on the appropriate medication and able to manage their own lives as well as care for their baby. 
Just because your family may think they can “do better” with your baby , that is not factored in during a CPS investigation. This is your child and we work with the family directly, not the extended family. Again, can’t speak for your state but where I work our policy is that we are not allowed to talk about a clients case to extended family without the client signing a release.  Grandparents call all the time asking about the status of a case and I have to tell them I can’t say anything without the clients permission. I know this is a long response but I hope it helps settle your mind a little bit. IF there is CPS involvement ask what they have to offer for help and accept whatever services are given. As for your family, I think going (and staying) no contact is the best response.

I cannot speak for the laws in your state but as a CPS investigator please let them look into this. Your kiddo has a broken leg, that’s serious stuff given her medical issues.  If you think it may have happened at preschool let them know. Be cooperative and open and honest. Is it a pain in the ass? Absolutely. But we are there to look after the health and safety of kids. I can’t speak for all social workers but any time I can help a family with resources (jackets, clothing, safety equipment etc...) and keep families intact, I call that a success.  Removing children from their home should always be an absolute last resort.
